gaps.sentence: The committee ___ of eight members and two advisers.
gaps.explanation: 'Consist of' = be made up of; 'composes of' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: She has lived in this street ___ 2015.
gaps.hint: starting point of a period up to now
gaps.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the situation started and continues; 'for' is used with a length of time.

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: The ___ reason for the delay was the weather.
gaps.hint: adjective meaning main or most important
gaps.explanation: 'Principal' as an adjective means main or most important; 'principle' is a noun meaning a basic rule or belief.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: The new tax law will ___ every small business in the region.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb (to influence); 'effect' is normally the noun.

gaps.sentence: Please be ___ — the baby is sleeping.
gaps.explanation: 'Quiet' means making little or no noise; 'quite' is an adverb meaning fairly or completely.

gaps.sentence: Smoke could be seen ___ from the factory chimneys.
gaps.hint: the smoke goes up by itself — no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (no object) describes the smoke going up; 'raise' would need an object (raise something).
